title: Cyrus and the Inheritance
premise: When a fresh corpse is discovered in the flooded quarry outside Millbrook wearing clothes stolen from Juniper Okafor's own closet, the true-crime podcaster realizes the killer is staging the town's coldest case — the 1994 disappearance of her mother's best friend, Delia Marsh. As Juniper reopens the investigation, she discovers her late grandmother's house sits on land deeded through a forged inheritance that ties three founding families to Delia's murder. The killer is Cyrus Bellamy, the beloved retired sheriff who has spent thirty years protecting his daughter's secret: she witnessed the original crime as a child. In the quarry's final confrontation, Juniper chooses truth over vengeance, exposing the cover-up while sparing the now-elderly witness, and finally claims belonging not by blood or inheritance, but by telling the story honestly.
about_author: Sable Vasquez is the pen name of a former court stenographer who spent two decades transcribing small-town trials before turning to fiction. She writes mysteries about archives, memory, and the lies communities tell themselves, and lives somewhere within driving distance of a reservoir.

chapters.title: The Clothes in the Quarry
chapters.summary: Juniper Okafor, POV. Recording a mundane episode about Millbrook's 1994 cold case, Juniper is summoned when divers pull a body from the quarry dressed in her own missing clothes. Shock curdles into professional dread: someone knows her wardrobe, her routines, her podcast. Emotional beat: violation — the investigator becomes evidence.

chapters.title: Alphabetized Secrets
chapters.summary: Juniper, POV. Retreating to her archive of seven years of research, she finds a page from her grandmother's ledger missing — cut cleanly, recently. Sheriff's deputy Ray Okonkwo warns her off, but notes the victim wore a 1994-era watch engraved 'D.M.' Emotional beat: the past isn't dead; it's filed, waiting.

chapters.title: What Delia Wore Last
chapters.summary: Alternating POV: Juniper interviews elderly seamstress Hattie Boone, who dressed Delia Marsh the day she vanished. Hattie recalls a third person at the quarry that night but goes silent when her son enters. Emotional beat: fear passed down like an heirloom; witnesses become keepers.

chapters.title: The Deed in Grandmother's Name
chapters.summary: Juniper, POV. Digging into property records for an episode, she finds the Okafor land was transferred in 1995 via a signature her dying grandmother could not have written. The forged deed links two other founding families. Emotional beat: inheritance revealed as theft; home feels suddenly borrowed.

chapters.title: Cyrus at the Diner
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Retired Sheriff Cyrus Bellamy buys Juniper coffee, charming and paternal, gently steering her toward the theory that Delia ran away. That night someone ransacks her studio, taking only tapes from 1994. Emotional beat: warmth with teeth in it; the reader suspects what Juniper resists.

chapters.title: A Child Saw Everything
chapters.summary: Juniper, POV. A former classmate reveals that Cyrus's daughter, Ruthie, was at the quarry that night — a child who never spoke again about it and left town at eighteen. Juniper tracks Ruthie down in another state. Emotional beat: the horror reframes; the monster may be a father protecting a traumatized girl.

chapters.title: Ruthie's Silence
chapters.summary: Ruthie Bellamy, POV (first time). Now a hospice nurse, Ruthie admits she saw her father bury something at the quarry in 1994 and has been paying for silence ever since — but insists he wasn't the killer. Someone else was there, someone whose name she traded away to protect him. Emotional beat: complicity and love tangled beyond untangling.

chapters.title: Thirty Years of Alibis
chapters.summary: Juniper, POV. Cross-referencing alibis, she finds all three deed-holding families covered for each other the night Delia died — orchestrated by then-deputy Cyrus to shield Ruthie from testifying against her uncle, who struck Delia in a quarrel over the land. Emotional beat: the conspiracy was mercy, badly kept, rotting into menace.

chapters.title: The Quarry at Low Water
chapters.summary: Climax. Cyrus, exposed, lures Juniper to the quarry intending one last staged scene; Ruthie arrives and finally speaks the truth aloud, breaking thirty years of silence. Ray intervenes as Cyrus, rather than fight, walks to the waterline and waits to be arrested. Emotional beat: confession as release; the killer surrenders to the story being told.

chapters.title: Belonging, Filed Under O
chapters.summary: Juniper, POV. Months later, her final episode airs unredacted; Ruthie, spared prosecution as a coerced witness, returns to Millbrook. Juniper refiles her archive under new names — including her own — and hangs her grandmother's restored deed on the wall. Emotional beat: found family and honest memory; the case closes, the podcaster comes home.
